metadata.description: SOLICITATION NUMBER: 0002018699 INSTITUTION: IBRD/IDA ASSIGNMENT LOCATION: Senegal ISSUE DATE AND TIME: Oct 02,2025 05:14 CLOSING DATE AND TIME: Oct 16,2025 23:59 Le Sénégal dispose d'un potentiel considérable en énergies renouvelables; y compris le solaire; en raison de sa situation géographique. Pour réduire sa dépendance aux combustibles fossiles importés; le Sénégal a choisi de diversifier ses sources d'énergie?: En fin 2024; 29 % de la puissance installée est de source renouvelable. Le pays vise une part de 40 % d’énergie renouvelable dans la capacité totale installée d'ici 2030. Bien que le Sénégal possède un potentiel considérable en matière de solaire photovoltaïque; il manque actuellement une stratégie définitive décrivant la contribution de l’autoproduction aux objectifs en matière d'énergies renouvelables. En parallèle; le gouvernement du Sénégal; dans le cadre de sa politique énergétique; s’est engagé à développer les énergies renouvelables. Cet engagement est notamment décliné dans le pacte national pour l’énergie avec l’objectif ‘’d’augmenter la part actuelle des énergies renouvelables dans le bouquet de production à 40%’’. Le développement de l’autoproduction d’origine renouvelable entre en droite ligne avec cet objectif. La mission a pour objet d'entreprendre une évaluation préliminaire du marché potentiel de l’autoproduction solaire; en mettant l'accent sur trois segments : i) bâtiments publics non couverts par les programmes décidés ; (ii) les immeubles résidentiels ; et iii) bâtiments commerciaux (y compris les usines; industries et les PME). Cette évaluation contribuera à éclairer la politique du ministère de l'Énergie; du Pétrole et des Mines (MEPM) relative à l’autoproduction d’origine photovoltaïque; les réglementations et programmes; ainsi que les mécanismes de financement potentiels dans ce secteur.

metadata.description: SOLICITATION NUMBER: 0002018523 INSTITUTION: IBRD/IDA , IFC , MIGA , ICSID ASSIGNMENT LOCATION: Tanzania ISSUE DATE AND TIME: Oct 03,2025 05:11 CLOSING DATE AND TIME: Oct 16,2025 23:59 In the Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar; the President’s Office Constitution; Legal Affairs; Public Service and Good Governance (POCLPG) has the responsibility of managing human resource information of public servants; while the President’s Office Finance and Planning (POFP); through its budget department; is tasked with payroll processing. As part of the digital transformation effort; the Government has designed and developed a web-based HR and Payroll System (HR-PayMIS) to improve efficiency; accountability and transparency in managing Government HR and payroll operations. The purpose of establishment of this system is to eliminate the existing challenge of the lack of accurate information of public servants and repeated incidences of inclusion of ghost workers in the Government payment system. The new system went live in February 2025; and has several modules; include an Operational Module; Salary Management Module; Deduction Module; Personal Information Module; Budget Module and others. Currently the system performs payroll processing; manages salary budgets; maintains employee personal information and loan management for approximately 43;292 public servants and is integrated with Zanzibar ID; ZSSF; Zanzibar Civil Status Registration Agency (ZCSRA). The HR-PAYMIS initiative is firmly anchored in the Zanzibar Development Vision 2050; which identifies digital transformation as a key pillar for elevating the archipelago to an upper-middle-income economy; and fully aligns with the upcoming Zanzibar Digital Policy; which mandates the use of digital technologies to ensure timely; effective; and cost-efficient public service delivery. As emphasized by the Zanzibar Digital Government Strategy (ZDGS) 2023–2027; systems like HR-PAYMIS; along with E-Office and ZanAjira; are transformative tools intended to streamline public administration; strengthen public finance management; and enhance overall governance efficiency. Improving and deploying HR-PAYMIS is therefore central to modernizing public service delivery in Zanzibar and is a core ambition of the POCLPG. By digitizing HR and payroll systems; the Government aims to unlock efficiency; transparency; and responsiveness—a foundational step toward realizing Vision 2050’s development trajectory and reinforcing POCLPG’s institutional modernization mandate. Despite the positive implementation progress to date; there have been some challenges and issues raised by various stakeholders regarding the performance; data accuracy; system integration; user roles and budget management controls of HR-PayMIS. There is also a need to assess data security; reliability; and scalability of the current system to ensure sustainability and alignment with international good practices. As such; the POCLPG; with support from the World Bank and the Government to Person (G2PX) Initiative; intends to address these challenges and inform future priorities for improvement and reform. This assignment will contribute by conducting a comprehensive review of the HR-PayMIS; providing recommendations for strengthening; upgrading; or re-engineering the system.

Achieving this goal relies on the systematic development of both technical and behavioral competencies through a comprehensive training framework; applicable to both newly onboard and existing personnel.The integration of Non-Conventional Renewable Energy Sources (NCRES) and Distributed Energy Resources (DER) as part of the ongoing energy transition has introduced new dynamic behaviors; increased variability; bidirectional power flows and other phenomena within the Colombian Interconnected System (SIN). Also; electrical power system resilience criteria required new competencies oriented to respond and recover quickly from disruptions and disruptions. These challenges have brought about significant changes to traditional grid operation; requiring advanced system modeling; real-time monitoring; and adaptive control strategies. As a result; it is essential to develop and maintain a technically specialized workforce capable of assimilating new grid codes; leveraging digital tools; and applying robust operational practices to ensure system reliability; stability; and resilience under increasingly complex operating conditions.A key factor in this capability is the implementation of structured training and competency management systems. These ensure that personnel involved in mission-critical processes maintain the technical and behavioral skills necessary to support secure; resilient; and reliable grid operations. Furthermore; continuous training supports effective change management in dynamic operational environments; aligning workforce capabilities with the integration of advanced technologies; evolving regulatory frameworks; and growing system complexity operational requirements. This approach not only strengthens knowledge retention and practical application but also drives talent development and organizational adaptability.In this context; XM recognizes that ensuring operational security requires a highly qualified and trained workforce; capable of managing the SIN with reliability; flexibility; and economic efficiency. The goal is to establish the organization as a regional benchmark for supervising and controlling high-renewable energy systems. New criteria applied are required due to resilience under NCRES; DERs and new technologies connected to the electrical power system. To meet this challenge; National Dispatch Center (CND; in Spanish) must be equipped of a specialized Operator Training Center. In collaboration with the World Bank and international donors–including the governments of Canada; Switzerland; the United Kingdom; and the United States–the MDTF provided financial and technical resources to help rebuild safer homes and offer socio-technical support.Over time; the MDTF expanded its focus to further enhance Nepal’s capacity for disaster resilience; addressing areas such as multi-hazard risk-assessment; resilient infrastructure; community preparedness; and disaster risk communication and awareness. In March 2023; the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA); the Department of Urban Development and Building Construction (DUDBC); MDTF Development Partners; and the World Bank agreed to advance activities to reinforce disaster risk reduction and management systems in Nepal for longer-term resilience. As part of the ongoing dialogue with municipalities; local governments have requested support to enhance their risk communication capacity. They emphasized that community preparedness and awareness are significant challenges in implementing disaster risk management efforts. In response to this request; the MDTF is developing a series of games to communicate key concepts from the field of disaster risk management. The games should be designed to help participants understand key disaster risk concepts and to explore practical strategies for reducing disaster risk in Nepal.Systems games such as these have the capacity to act as flight simulators for decision-makers; helping to illuminate key trade-offs; support collaboration and negotiation; and develop skills in making decisions under time constraints. The games should cover a wide range of disaster risk management (DRM) concepts for a broad spectrum of participants; including government officials; community members; construction engineers; entrepreneurs and NGOs. These Terms of Reference (TOR) have been prepared to implement the activity under the MDTF resilient infrastructure pillar; with the aim of scaling up nationwide institutional capacity to deliver interactive performances that promote disaster preparedness and raise public awareness. To co-design and facilitate a program to train artists and community organizers from around Nepal in innovative techniques for communicating DRM principles.

For persons with disabilities and veterans; interviews will explore personal employment histories and lived experiences during job search; recruitment; onboarding; and navigating services or workplace environments. The discussions will also address experiences perceived enablers and obstacles to meaningful inclusion; barriers to employment; experience with stigma; and how disability- or veteran-specific needs were met.The qualitative findings will be framed into the current social and policy context by desk review of relevant literature; regulations; policy documents; and into a review of available secondary data. metadata.description: SOLICITATION NUMBER: 0002018597 INSTITUTION: IBRD/IDA ASSIGNMENT LOCATION: Colombia ISSUE DATE AND TIME: Sep 29,2025 05:13 CLOSING DATE AND TIME: Oct 07,2025 23:59 Colombia has significant renewable energy potential; with particular interest in offshore wind power in the Caribbean region. This innovative energy source could not only strengthen the electricity sector but also boost port development; generate employment; contribute to decarbonization; and foster science and technology. Harnessing this potential requires effective coordination among market participants and public entities responsible for energy; environmental; and social interests; as well as careful infrastructure planning; risk management; and administrative synchronization to facilitate energy development.The Mines and Energy Planning Unit (UPME) prepares the National Energy Plan (PEN); a long-term roadmap identifying potential pathways for a sustainable energy transition in Colombia. It is also responsible for the Reference Generation and Transmission Expansion Plan (PERGT); which is indicative for generation and mandatory for transmission. While the PEN covers a 30-year horizon; the PERGT focuses on a 15-year timeframe; prioritizing the expansion projects needed to ensure a secure and reliable energy supply; maximizing user benefits. For coordinated planning; the PEN must identify strategic investments that will be evaluated in detail by the PERGT; especially in electric infrastructure.One of the critical challenges in implementing these plans is the need to align mandatory decisions with public policies to mitigate risks associated with infrastructure delays; implementation difficulties by project developers; and economic; social; and environmental externalities. Traditionally; system expansion planning has been based on a hydrothermal context; but it now requires adaptation to incorporate renewable energy sources (FNCER) effectively into a diversified matrix. The Caribbean region; in particular; presents high offshore wind potential; but its integration will require transmission projects in the STN and STR systems; adding complexity to the planning process. High uncertainty in project execution calls for updating the PERGT’s deterministic methodology; allowing for a more flexible approach that assesses diverse and realistic energy scenarios. To address these challenges; UPME is modernizing the PEN with an alternative optimization approach and will launch the "Flexibility Technologies in the Electricity Sector" project; introducing advanced methodologies for flexibility assessment in planning and a computational evaluation tool.In response to these challenges; the World Bank supports UPME in harmonizing planning methodologies to integrate Non-Conventional Renewable Energy Sources (FNCER) into Colombia's energy matrix. This support focuses on updating the PERGT and improving the integration between the PEN and PERGT to identify strategic benefits and quantify their impact on the country’s energy sector.

metadata.description: SOLICITATION NUMBER: 0002018270 INSTITUTION: IBRD/IDA ASSIGNMENT LOCATION: Bangladesh; Bhutan; Sri Lanka; Maldives; Nepal ISSUE DATE AND TIME: Sep 25,2025 05:09 CLOSING DATE AND TIME: Oct 06,2025 23:59 The Plastic Free Rivers and Seas for South Asia (PLEASE) project; implemented by the South Asia Co-operative Environment Program (SACEP) with support from the World Bank; addresses the urgent need for coordinated action against plastic pollution in South Asia. 1. Plastic pollution in South Asia is a transboundary challenge; with rivers carrying waste across borders and into the ocean; making national efforts alone insufficient. Regional cooperation is essential for harmonizing policies; sharing knowledge; and coordinating action among countries facing similar pressures from rising plastic consumption and mismanaged waste. By bringing together governments; industry; and civil society; the assignment proposed building a foundation for a standardized regional action plan; enabling countries to identify hotspots collectively; align on solutions; and leverage public-private partnerships for greater impact.II. Sri Lanka faces ongoing challenges with plastic waste; as the country’s recycling rate remains low and industries often prefer cheaper virgin plastics over recycled materials. The plastic value chain is characterized by limited infrastructure and inconsistent quality standards; which makes it challenging for recycled products to compete.III. Nepal’s plastic waste management system is still developing; especially for non-PET plastics like LDPE and multi-layer packaging. Much of this waste is not collected or recycled; leading to pollution in rivers that flow downstream into neighbouring countries. Mapping the flow of problematic plastics and analyzing market barriers is crucial to guiding policy reforms and infrastructure improvements.IV. Bangladesh has seen a rapid increase in plastic use; particularly in urban areas. While the government has set ambitious targets for recycling and reducing single-use plastics; the country’s waste management infrastructure is struggling to keep up. Many recycling operations remain small-scale and rely heavily on informal workers. A comprehensive review of existing infrastructure; value chain analysis; and assessment of industry readiness for new regulations; such as EPR; will identify investment needs and opportunities for more effective business models to support Bangladesh’s transition to a circular economy and enhance working conditions in the sector.V. The Maldives is known for its beach tourism; which is a major contributor to the national economy. However; marine plastic pollution poses a threat to both the environment and the tourism industry. Despite new policies; enforcement and infrastructure for managing single-use plastics are limited. The assignment will focus on developing a framework for achieving Blue Flag Beach accreditation; which involves selecting pilot sites; engaging stakeholders; and aligning efforts with national tourism and waste management strategies.VI. Bhutan’s urban centers; such as Thimphu and Paro; generate significant amounts of plastic waste; much of which ends up in rivers that flow into neighbouring countries. Waste management systems are still evolving; and there is a reliance on informal workers and open burning. The assignment will review the effectiveness of current policies and incentives; identify gaps; and suggest practical steps for improving the EPR framework. By focusing on fiscal and infrastructure solutions; the work supports Bhutan’s efforts to reduce plastic leakage and promote cleaner; more sustainable cities.Objectives of the AssignmentThe objective of this assignment is to strengthen regional and national capacity to reduce plastic pollution in South Asia by supporting the development of a harmonized regional action plan under SACEP; and by conducting targeted country-level diagnostics and interventions to improve policy; infrastructure; and market systems for effective EPR implementation and integrate private sector led circular economy solutions for plastics in Sri Lanka; Nepal; Bangladesh; Maldives; and Bhutan.

metadata.content: Fused PNT Analyses based on European Infrastructure
metadata.description: The European Commission is launching a study on the potential use of communication-oriented LEO constellations for the deployment of a complementary PNT service. This approach is normally referred to as Fused PNT. This tender will focus on developing a user terminal prototype and a simulated environment enabling to assess the performance of Fused PNT under a realistic set of propagation conditions and inter-satellite interference. In this procurement, the main goals of the European Commission are: • To develop a software receiver, supporting acquisition and tracking of 3GPP reference signals for Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) • To model multipath channel and intersatellite interference, in order to test the software receiver under the realistic satellite based propagation channel and interferences; • To consolidate and complement the part of the E2E emulator, by adding multipath and intersatellite interference models; • To demonstrate the performance of fused PNT ranging in a representative simulated environment • To validate the acquisition and tracking performance in realistic environment.

metadata.description: JRC Geel is located 7 km outside Geel centre and is not well connected to the public transport infrastructure. JRC Geel members of staff undertake numerous missions during the year in connection to the business needs of the institute. Additionally there is a large number of visitors visiting the JRC Geel on a regular and non-regular basis. The transport services are mainly provided within the boundaries of the provinces of Antwerpen, Limburg and Vlaams-Brabant (incl. Brussels). Occasionally the services are required outside the areas mentioned above and include transport abroad (for example Germany, the Netherlands) depending on the relevant activities of the JRC Geel. The main destinations are to / from the Brussels airport, to/from Brussels centre and to/from Geel / Mol. Therefore, the JRC Geel has an intention to call upon an external service provider for the transport of staff members and visitors of the JRC Geel by car and minibus. Furthermore, transport of luggage with normal weight and size is also required.

metadata.description: Eurostat Unit B3-Enlargement, neighbourhood and development cooperation is launching this call for tenders in order to seek assistance from external contractors to organise meetings under two lots. Lot 1 involves organising three High-Level Seminars, participation in two Quality Conferences, and attendance of 30 total participants in events indicated by Eurostat, for the European Neighbourhood Policy-East and Central Asian countries over 3 years of the contract duration. Lot 2 involves organising three Forum meetings, participation in two Quality Conferences, and organising six total Principal National Coordinators and Working Group meetings back-to-back with a workshop, of which 3 on-site and 3 on-line for the European Neighbourhood Policy-South countries over 3 years of the contract duration. Eurostat pursues long-standing statistical cooperation with the Eastern Neighbourhood and Central Asia countries in the framework of the European Neighbourhood Policy and EU’s policy in Central Asia. The cooperation covers Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus , Georgia, Moldova, and Ukraine. Additionally, Eurostat pursues long-standing statistical cooperation with the Southern Neighbourhood partners in the framework of the European Neighbourhood Policy. The cooperation covers Algeria, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Palestine , Syria, and Tunisia. The main purpose of the statistical cooperation support provided to the partner countries is for them to enhance their statistical capacities and produce reliable and timely official statistics. For these data to be comparable with EU statistics, it is essential that the partner countries' National Statistical Institutes (NSIs) are aware of the latest developments and best practices in the field of statistics. This will require regular exchange of information and guidance on key issues and developments in the field of statistics, as well as opportunities for networking and collaboration with EU statistical experts. Most of the NSIs in the region lack the opportunities for regular high-level discussions and exchange of experiences with their EU counterparts, which is crucial for advancing their statistical systems and aligning them with EU and international standards. The envisaged contract duration for each lot is 36 months. The implementation of each lot will start on 1 January 2026.

metadata.content: Study on modern pricing and risks of collusion
metadata.description: DG COMP is working on a follow-up to the comprehensive 2024 report: “Protecting competition in a changing world: Evidence on the evolution of competition in the EU during the past 25 years”. This report identified important changes over the past 25 years in the competitive environment (rising concentration, markups and profits, declining business dynamism). It also identified a number of likely structural and institutional drivers of those changes (rise of intangible investments, globalisation, regulation and M&A). The 2024 report did however not explore whether changes in management practices (strategies and tactics) may also have contributed to some of the detected trends. The present study seeks to address this gap by exploring whether the rise of modern pricing and revenue management strategies and tactics may have partly contributed to some of the observed changes in the competitive environment, inter alia by increasing the risk of collusion.

Im Zusammenhang mit Neubauprojekten, bei dem die technischen Anlagen ab Ende 2025 eingebaut und im Jahr 2028 in Betrieb genommen werden sollen, wird der Rechtsbeistand beigezogen, um mögliche Ansprüche der Auftragnehmer aus rechtlicher Sicht zu identifizieren, auf Anforderung zu bewerten und das JRC Karlsruhe bei verschiedenen Tätigkeiten zu unterstützen, wie z. B:

•	Beratung zu Strategien zur Schadensminderung
•	Identifizierung potenzieller Ansprüche (im Falle von Verzögerungen, Änderungen, unvorhergesehenen Bedingungen usw. bei der Vertragsausführung) und Analyse von Ursache-Wirkungs-Beziehungen
•	Bewertung von eingereichten Nachtragsforderungen auf vertragsrechtliche Ansprüche
•	Abwehr und Verhandlung etwaiger außergerichtlichen Ansprüche 
•	Prüfung, Vorbereitung und Einreichung von Mängel- und Schadensersatzansprüchen.

Der Berater für Rechtsfragen soll zudem das JRC Karlsruhe unterstützen bei Aufgaben wie z. B:
